brief_rationale: The doctor systematically screens for current fever/infection/bleeding, reconciles licorine/leucogen tablets at 20 mg TID, establishes a named hematology/oncology follow-up owner and near-term CBC plan, verifies home-monitoring feasibility by quietly eliciting the caregiver's role, obtains explicit teach-back on urgent-return thresholds, and grounds all advice in workspace discharge records while labeling unknowns. No responsibility-chain error exists. High-order points HO1 (plain caregiver-facing language turning cytopenia into concrete home actions), HO3 (record-gathering plan linking fragmented outside-hospital chemotherapy/LP/intrathecal records to care continuity), and HO4 (repairing the incomplete follow-up bridge by assigning owner and caregiver-owned tasks before contact) are actively completed with meaningful trajectory impact, but HO2 remains partial because the doctor only reinforces the privacy-safe disclosure that the family already offered without further targeted exploration, and HO1's completion is constrained by not fully checking the caregiver's comfort with the planned psychiatric disclosure. The trajectory therefore satisfies Strong but not Perfect.
